questions.stem:
The most fascinating thing of all was the bus
that travelled between her village and the nearest
town. It passed through her street each hour, once
going to the town and once coming back. The sight
of the bus, filled each time with a new set of
passengers, was a source of unending joy for Valli.
Day after day she watched the bus, and
gradually a tiny wish crept into her head and
grew there: she wanted to ride on that bus, even
if just once. This wish became stronger and
stronger, until it was an overwhelming desire.

Day after day Valli watches the same bus pass her street, and the wish to ride in it keeps growing stronger. What does this show about her? (A) That she is easily put off by small difficulties (B) That she waits for others to decide for her (C) That the wish to ride the bus had become the strongest thing in her mind (D) That she is far more interested in the town than in the journey itself

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: You are travelling by yourself from your village to the nearest town and will be back before four in the afternoon. Write a message of about 100 words to your mother telling her where you are going, when you will be back, and how you will pay for the ticket.

markingPoints.description: Content: names the town and gives the timing of the trip, reaching the town at one forty-five and coming back by about two forty-five
Content: explains the payment, thirty paise to the town and another thirty paise to return, out of the sixty paise saved
Format: written as a message, with a greeting at the start and a closing at the end
Organisation: the points run in a sensible order, where she is going, when she will be back, how she will pay, and a final reassurance
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling and punctuation, with short sentences joined into connected writing

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Dear Mother, I am going to the town this afternoon. I will take the one o'clock bus, reach the town at one forty-five and come back on the same bus by about two forty-five. I will be home long before four. Please do not worry about me. I have sixty paise saved, so I can pay thirty paise for the ticket there and another thirty paise to come back. I have not touched the money in the tin. I will take my own ticket and keep it safe. Your loving daughter, Valli

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Write an advertisement of about 100 words for your village notice board about the bus that runs between the village and the nearest town. Give the timings, the fare and the time the journey takes.

markingPoints.description: Content: states that the bus runs every hour, once to the town and once back
Content: gives the distance of six miles, the journey time of forty-five minutes and the fare of thirty paise one way
Content: mentions that another thirty paise brings the passenger home on the same bus
Format: written as an advertisement, with a bold heading and short lines of advertising copy
Organisation, accuracy and expression: the facts are given in a clear order, with correct spelling, punctuation and joined sentences

answerScheme.modelAnswer: BUS SERVICE: VILLAGE TO TOWN. A bus runs between this village and the nearest town every hour, once towards the town and once coming back. The town is six miles from the village and the trip takes forty-five minutes. The fare is thirty paise one way. If you stay in your seat at the town, you can return home on the same bus by paying another thirty paise. The one o'clock afternoon bus reaches the town at one forty-five and brings you back by about two forty-five. All are welcome to travel. Buy your ticket from the conductor and keep it safe.

evidence:

going to the town and once coming back.
The town was six miles from her village.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A friend of yours says that a bus journey is boring because nothing happens on the road. Write a paragraph of about 100 words on 'What a traveller can watch from a fast-moving bus', using the sights you have seen from a moving vehicle.

markingPoints.description: Content: lists the sights seen from the window, such as rivers, green fields, hills, roadside shops and market places
Content: includes railway tracks, moving trains and vehicles on the road
Content: mentions trees, a crowd, clothes in shops and animals on the road
Format and organisation: one continuous paragraph, not a list, with a clear opening and a closing sentence
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling and punctuation, with sentences of different lengths joined smoothly

answerScheme.modelAnswer: A fast-moving bus shows a traveller far more than the road ahead. From the window one can see rivers, green fields and hills, and roadside shops and market places going by. Railway tracks run along the ground, and moving trains keep pace with the bus. Vehicles on the road appear and vanish in a moment. Trees seem to come running towards the bus and then stand still by the roadside. One can also see a crowd, clothes in shops and animals on the road. Even a vehicle that seems about to be swallowed by the bus passes on smoothly, and every view is a new one before the next begins.

(3) The road is very narrow, with the canal, palm trees, grassland, distant mountains and blue sky on one side, a deep ditch and green fields on the other. (4) Trees seem to run towards the bus and then stand helplessly by the roadside. (5) The bus seems on the point of gobbling up another vehicle or a pedestrian, yet passes on smoothly. (6) A galloping cow and a train rushing past the crossing gate with a tremendous roar and rattle fill her with delight.
